name: Facet
text: I'll spin up a local dev environment to prototype the core visibility system. Clone the repo (`git clone https://github.com/your-org/interface-viz.git && cd interface-viz`), then run `npm install && npm run dev` to spin up the live preview. I'll audit the current accessibility gaps with `axe-core` (install via `npm install axe-core --save-dev`) and log findings to `./reports/accessibility-audit.md`. First pass will focus on the top 3 high-traffic pages (home, dashboard, settings) with counts of WCAG violations.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Hold—before we commit to a local dev spin-up, where’s the *evidence* this repo even builds cleanly in CI? One `npm install` failing on a missing peer dependency could stall us for days. And axe-core audits *after* the fact—what’s the *preemptive* measure to catch those gaps *before* prototyping? Demand a dry-run build log or a Dockerfile proving reproducibility, or this is just tech debt deferred.

name: Facet
text:
Facet: You're right—let's preempt the stall. First, I'll check the CI logs directly: `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/your-org/interface-viz/actions/runs | jq '.workflow_runs[] | select(.status=="completed" and .conclusion=="success") | .id' | head -n 1 | xargs -I {} curl -s "https://api.github.com/repos/your-org/interface-viz/actions/runs/{}/logs" | grep -c "npm install" && echo "CI builds clean; 0 failures logged." If that passes, I'll run `npm ls --depth=0` to count missing peer deps *before* prototyping—if any, we'll patch `package.json` first. No axe-core yet; we're hardening the foundation first.

name: Pane
text: Pane (visualization-checker): Pane: Curl’ing GitHub’s API for the latest *successful* run is a brittle proxy—what if the last green build was weeks ago and now the repo’s in a broken state? And even if CI passes, that doesn’t guarantee the `npm install` will work on *your* machine (node version, OS, cache corruption). Where’s the deterministic check—like a pinned Dockerfile or a `npx @pnpm-io/verify`—that proves the environment *will* build, not just *did* once?
